title: Search and Indexing Implementation Reference
readerIntent: Locate provider-family ownership, configuration, source contracts, and focused tests.
priorKnowledge: Understand the search-model and provider architecture.
summary: nSearch owns the family boundary, search owns provider-neutral behavior, and elastic owns Elasticsearch-specific integration.

sections.heading: Normalized search contract
items: nSearch defines index lifecycle, document operations, query, pagination, bulk, refresh, alias, health, error, and provider selection contracts.
Business modules own search models and index declarations; adapters map those contracts to Elasticsearch or future engines without becoming business authority.
Callers supply approved provider-neutral queries and never raw engine DSL, connection clients, arbitrary index names, or credentials.

sections.heading: Configuration and capabilities
items: Properties configure active provider, endpoints, TLS, secret reference, indexes, timeouts, retries, bulk limits, refresh, aliases, and engine-specific approved options.
Adapters register truthful support for analyzers, mappings, aliases, vector search, highlighting, aggregation, pagination, and operational lifecycle.
Elasticsearch local development configuration does not establish production clustering, security, backup, capacity, compatibility, or upgrade qualification.

sections.heading: Index and query lifecycle
items: Create candidate mappings, populate from authorized source models, validate counts and samples, activate aliases, retain rollback, and retire old indexes by policy.
Import finalization and ordinary mutations index only after authoritative persistence; failures create recoverable derived-state work rather than repeating business writes blindly.
Queries enforce tenant, permission, field projection, bounded page/size, stable sorting, timeout, and provider-neutral error behavior.

sections.heading: Qualification and operations
items: Test mapping, analyzer, CRUD, bulk, query, sort, pagination, alias, rebuild, tenant isolation, masking, outage, retry, partial batch, and recovery.
Qualify live security, TLS, credentials, load, shards, replicas, disk, snapshots, restore, rolling upgrade, supported versions, and failure modes.
Monitor query latency, errors, zero results, indexing throughput and lag, rejected work, cluster state, alias state, disk, and rebuild progress.

sections.heading: Ownership
items: gFramework/nSearch: family ownership and provider selection guidance.
gFramework/nSearch/search: normalized routes, services, pipelines, models, cache, and errors.
gFramework/nSearch/elastic: Elasticsearch connection, mappings, operations, and client calls.
Owning business modules: schemas and src/search/indexes.js definitions.
Project/environment layers: provider activation and deployment configuration.

sections.heading: Focused tests
paragraphs: Record engine, adapter, mapping, topology, volume, security mode, and qualification results so provider claims remain reproducible.
